scenario: A curator is arranging six sculptures—Garnet, Helios, Ironwood, Juno, Kestrel, and Lyra—along a single gallery corridor, placing each sculpture at exactly one of six consecutive pedestals numbered 1 through 6 from the entrance. The arrangement must conform to the following conditions: Garnet is placed at a pedestal numbered lower than Juno's. Helios is placed immediately before or immediately after Kestrel. Ironwood is not placed at pedestal 1 or pedestal 6. Lyra is placed at some pedestal after Kestrel. Juno is not placed immediately next to Kestrel.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be an acceptable arrangement of the sculptures, from pedestal 1 to pedestal 6?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Garnet, Juno, Helios, Kestrel, Ironwood, Lyra

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ironwood, Garnet, Helios, Kestrel, Juno, Lyra

choices.label: C
choices.text: Garnet, Helios, Kestrel, Juno, Ironwood, Lyra

choices.label: D
choices.text: Juno, Garnet, Kestrel, Helios, Ironwood, Lyra

choices.label: E
choices.text: Garnet, Juno, Kestrel, Ironwood, Helios, Lyra

explanations.correct: Garnet(1) before Juno(2) ✓; Helios(3) adjacent to Kestrel(4) ✓; Ironwood at 5, not 1 or 6 ✓; Kestrel(4) before Lyra(6) ✓; Juno(2) not adjacent to Kestrel(4) ✓.
explanations.B: Ironwood is at pedestal 1, violating the rule that Ironwood is not at pedestal 1 or 6.
explanations.C: Juno(4) is adjacent to Kestrel(3), violating the Juno–Kestrel non-adjacency rule.
explanations.D: Garnet(2) is not before Juno(1); violates the Garnet–Juno ordering rule.
explanations.E: Helios(5) is not adjacent to Kestrel(3); violates the Helios–Kestrel adjacency rule.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: Lyra must come after Kestrel, and Ironwood cannot be at pedestal 6. Testing all eight worlds confirms Lyra occupies pedestal 6 in every solution.
explanations.A: Garnet is at pedestal 2 in some solutions.
explanations.C: Ironwood is at pedestal 4 in some solutions.
explanations.E: Juno can be at pedestal 1, 2, 4, or 5.

questions.questionStem: If Juno is placed at pedestal 2, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: If Juno is at 2, then Garnet (which must precede Juno) must be at pedestal 1.
explanations.B: Helios can be at pedestal 3 or 4 when Juno is at 2.
explanations.C: Kestrel can be at pedestal 3 or 4.
explanations.D: Ironwood is at pedestal 5 when Juno is at 2.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

explanations.correct: If Kestrel were at pedestal 5, then Helios would need to be at pedestal 4 or 6 (adjacency), and Lyra would need a pedestal after 5—forcing Lyra to 6 and Helios to 4. But Juno cannot be adjacent to Kestrel, so Juno cannot be at 4 or 6, leaving Juno at 1, 2, or 3. However, Ironwood must take one of 2 or 3 (not 1 or 6), and Garnet must precede Juno. Working through placements, no valid arrangement satisfies all constraints.
explanations.A: Juno at 1 occurs in a verified solution (with Garnet at 2).
explanations.B: Kestrel at 2 occurs in a verified solution.
explanations.C: Ironwood at 4 occurs in verified solutions.
explanations.D: Helios at 4 occurs in verified solutions.
explanations.E: Correct—no valid arrangement places Kestrel at pedestal 5.

questions.questionStem: If Ironwood is placed at pedestal 4, then which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: With Ironwood at 4, two verified solutions apply: Garnet=1, Helios=2, Kestrel=3, Juno=5, Lyra=6; and Garnet=1, Helios=3, Kestrel=2, Juno=5, Lyra=6. Both place Juno at pedestal 5.
explanations.A: Juno must be at pedestal 5 in both applicable worlds; it cannot be at 1.
explanations.E: Lyra is at pedestal 6 in both applicable worlds.
